newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* Ford Motor Co said it plans to manufacture 250,000 vehicles that would run on either ethanol or gasoline.
* The German government has reversed itself and is abandoning plans to cut its budget deficit by revaluing gold reserves, a move that had been opposed by the Bundesbank.

* The General Accounting Office is expected to testify in favour of AMR Corp's American Airlines and British Airways Plc cutting back on the number of landing rights it has at London's Heathrow Airport.
* The Conference Board reported a drop of one-tenth of one percent in the index of leading indicators.
* The Dow Jones industrials average closed up 22.75 points, resting at 7312.15.
* American Management Systems Inc chief executive Charles Rossotti has been tapped by the Clinton administration to head the Internal Revenue Service.
* The Mexican government set economic policy goals through to 2000.
* Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto offered a plan to cut spending in the next fiscal year by one-half of one percent.
* PepsiCo Inc has to regroup in the wake of the departure of John Antioco, president and chief executive of its Taco Bell unit.
* American stock markets are moving closer to the day when they are based on actual dollars and cents, rather than fractions.
* Viacom Inc named a new chief executive of its struggling Blockbuster video unit, recruiting a man known for tackling tough tasks.
* Chicago exchanges are looking to loosen the grip of federal regulations on the way they conduct business.
* McDonald's Corp put a stop to its 55-cent sandwich promotion at lunch and dinner, a campaign that had been widely criticised by franchisees.
